originalTitle: Indel Money to raise up to Rs 500 crore via public issue of NCDs
simplifiedContent: Indel Money is planning to raise money from the public by issuing non-convertible debentures (NCDs), which are a type of investment where you lend money to the company. The company hopes to raise up to Rs 500 crore, and people can invest in these NCDs from August 18 to August 31. The money raised will be used for various purposes, including lending to others and paying off existing debts. This public issue is an opportunity for individual investors to lend money to Indel Money and earn interest in return. The issue may close early if the company reaches its target, so investors should act within the given timeframe.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know about the stock market news: Indian stock markets had a bad day, with many stocks losing value. This was partly because the leader of the Tata Group, N Chandrasekaran, is leaving his role at Tata Sons, which caused Tata Group stocks to fall. The price of crude oil is also getting close to $90, which is making people worry about inflation. As a result, the Sensex (a key stock market index) fell by 188 points and the Nifty (another important index) fell by 36 points. Overall, it was a tough day for the stock market, although some areas like banks and metals did a little better.

originalTitle: US stocks: CoreWeave, Super Micro surge on signs of sustained AI buildout
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in simple terms: Two companies, CoreWeave and Super Micro, have seen their stock prices go up a lot lately. This is because many people think that Artificial Intelligence (AI) will keep growing and these companies make the technology needed to support it. CoreWeave and Super Micro have both said they expect to make more money than previously thought, which makes investors happy and confident. This is a big deal because it shows that investors believe AI will continue to be an important area of growth, which is why they're buying more stocks in these companies. As a result, the stock prices of CoreWeave and Super Micro have reached new highs.

originalTitle: IRCTC Q1 Results: Revenue rises 18%, profit remains largely flat at  ₹330 crore
simplifiedContent: IRCTC, a company that operates train services and tourism, recently shared its financial results for the first quarter. The company's revenue, or total income, increased by 18% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹1,369.53 crore. However, its profit remained almost the same as last year, at ₹330.16 crore. This is because while some parts of the business, like catering, did well, others, like tourism, didn't perform as strongly. Overall, the company's income grew, but its profit didn't increase as much as might have been expected.

originalTitle: ‘Successor… not Warren’: Michael Burry says ‘Berkshire is no longer attractive’ over $400 billon cash pile concerns
simplifiedContent: A well-known investor named Michael Burry thinks that Berkshire Hathaway, a company led by Warren Buffett, is no longer a good investment. This is because the company has a large amount of cash, over $400 billion, that it hasn't been using. Since Warren Buffett is no longer in charge, the new CEO Greg Abel is starting to use this cash, but some people are still unsure if this is a good thing. This matters because it could affect the company's performance and the value of its shares. Berkshire Hathaway used to be a top performer in the market, but it has been struggling lately.

originalTitle: From Trent to Titan: Over 15 Tata Group stocks more than doubled investors' wealth during Chandrasekaran's tenure
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: many stocks (or company shares) owned by the Tata Group have increased a lot in value since N Chandrasekaran took charge. In fact, over 15 of these stocks have more than doubled in value, with some even increasing by over 1,000%. This means that people who invested in these stocks have made a lot of money. Chandrasekaran, who has been with the company for 40 years, has announced that he will be leaving his position as chairman in February 2027. This marks the end of his time in charge, during which the company's stocks have done very well.
